title: Mismatch and Coordinate-Correction Rejection
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $2^n$, and let $w,w_0$ be Boolean strings of length $n$. For a coordinate $j$, form its truth-table sign vector on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, and consider the local correction of the function obtained from $f$ by the coordinatewise binary-to-sign encoding, in the direction corresponding to that vector. If this correction equals the sign encoded by $w_0(j)$ with probability at least $1/2$ for a uniformly random point of the cube, then the probability that it fails to equal the sign encoded by $w(j)$ is at least $1/2$ when $w(j)\ne w_0(j)$, and is at least zero when they agree.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $2^n$
$w$ and $w_0$ are Boolean strings of length $n$
The coordinate-correction probability for $w_0(j)$ is at least $1/2$
